Series::softplus¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::softplus() const -> Series
Series::softplus(double beta, double threshold) const -> Series
Series& Series::softplus_() const

What It Does¶

softplus() is a smooth approximation of relu():

softplus(x) = (1 / beta) * log(1 + exp(beta * x))

With the default beta = 1 it is log(1 + exp(x)). The curve is always positive, is log(2) at x = 0, decays smoothly toward 0 for large negative x, and approaches the line y = x for large positive x. Increasing beta sharpens the bend so the shape converges on relu().

For numerical safety, once beta * x exceeds threshold (default 20) the function returns x directly — exp(beta * x) past that point is so large that (1/beta) * log(1 + exp(beta * x)) equals x to full precision anyway.

softplus() needs a floating-point input.

Parameters¶

beta (double, default 1)

Sharpness. Larger values make the transition tighter around x = 0.

threshold (double, default 20)

Above beta * x = threshold the output is x unchanged, to avoid overflow in exp.

Returns¶

Series The activated values, always positive, same shape and floating-point dtype as the input.

Gradient¶

softplus() is differentiable, and its derivative is a (scaled) sigmoid:

d/dx softplus(x) = sigmoid(beta * x)

With beta = 1 that is exactly sigmoid(x) — 0.5 at the origin, tending to 1 on the right and 0 on the left. Unlike relu(), the gradient is never exactly 0, so a softplus() unit stays trainable everywhere.

In-Place Form¶

softplus_() is the in-place sibling of softplus(): it computes the same result and writes it back into self directly — mutating it (and any other handle sharing the same storage) instead of allocating a new Series — then returns a reference to self.

Despite being declared const at the call site — a quirk of how this method’s wrapper is generated, not a promise that self is left unchanged — softplus_() genuinely mutates the series it’s called on.

auto x = pluss::make_series({0.0, 1.0});

auto& ref = x.softplus_();
std::cout << "x=" << x << "\n";
std::cout << std::boolalpha << "same object: " << (&ref == &x);

Output¶

x=pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[0.69314718, 1.3132617]
same object: true

Examples¶

Example 1. The default beta = 1 form, log(1 + exp(x)).

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0}).softplus());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0486, 0.3133, 0.6931, 1.3133, 3.0486]

softplus(0) = log(2) = 0.6931, and by x = 3 the output is already close to x.

Example 2. A larger beta sharpens the bend toward relu().

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0}).softplus(2.0, 20.0));

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0012, 0.0635, 0.3466, 1.0635, 3.0012]

At x = 0 the value is now log(2) / 2 = 0.3466, and the negative tail is pushed closer to 0.

Example 3. Past the threshold the output is exactly x.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({30.0, 50.0}).softplus());

Output¶

Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[30.0000, 50.0000]

Example 4. The backward is sigmoid(beta * x).

auto x = pluss::make_series({-3.0, -1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 3.0});
x.tracks_slope_(true);

x.softplus().sum().reverse();

pluss::series::print(std::cout, x.sensitivity());

Output¶

Series(shape=[5], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=5, contiguous=true)
data=[0.0474, 0.2689, 0.5000, 0.7311, 0.9526]

Those are sigmoid([-3, -1, 0, 1, 3]).

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The two-argument form takes beta and threshold together; there is no beta-only overload.

  • Floating-point input only; an integer series raises.

  • The output is strictly positive, so softplus() is not a drop-in for relu() where an exact 0 is required.

Summary¶

softplus(x) is a smooth, strictly positive relu():

  • (1/beta) * log(1 + exp(beta * x)), returning x once beta * x > threshold

  • floating-point input only

  • differentiable, backward sigmoid(beta * x) — never exactly 0

See Also¶

  • Series::relu: the non-smooth limit as beta -> inf.

  • Series::sigmoid: the derivative of softplus().

  • Series::logaddexp: softplus(x) is logaddexp(x, 0).
